transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Carlos (SynergiHealth Eng Manager), Priya (Head of Security), Liam (Cloud Eng), Ava (PM)

Summary:
Quick private/VPC discovery for SynergiHealth evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) vs Dedicated. Main topics: network connectivity options (VPC peering, PrivateLink/private endpoints), region constraints (EU data residency), egress/NAT, peering across accounts and cross-region limits, KMS/HSM and key management, audit logs and retention, approximate sizing for POC and pricing ask. Agreed next steps and action owners at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey all, thanks for joining, um we sent the calendar — i'll kick off, i'm jordan lee, i'm the account exec on this, maya our se is with me.
[00:06] Maya: hi everyone, maya here — se focused on private deployments and networking, happy to go deep.
[00:10] Carlos: hey thanks, carlos here, eng manager for inference platform, priya's on security and liam does our cloud infra.
[00:18] Priya: hi, quick ask — we need to validate KMS entitlements and SOC2 before moving to any demo, so that's top of our list.
[00:25] Jordan: totally, we'll share the security pack, SOC2, pen-test summary, and a redwood private network guide.
[00:30] Liam: great — high level, we run in eu-west-1 primarily, occasionally us-east-1, so we need to make sure data residency and cross-region traffic is minimized. also curious about private endpoints vs peering.
[00:42] Maya: yeah, good. quick lay of the land: Redwood Private can be deployed into your VPC using a few patterns — classic VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (private endpoints), or via Transit Gateway for multi-account setups. each has tradeoffs on route table complexity, cross-region support, and IP exhaustion.
[01:02] Carlos: can you do peering across accounts without transit gateway? we like keeping things simple.
[01:08] Maya: you can peer VPC-to-VPC across accounts in the same region — peering does not support transitive routing so if you have multiple VPCs you'd need either many peerings or TGW. PrivateLink (endpoint services) is easier for multi-account access and is what most customers pick for production because you get an ENI in each consumer VPC and you don't have to manage route tables as much.
[01:28] Priya: is PrivateLink supported in eu-west-3? sometimes the endpoints are limited by region.
[01:33] Maya: good call — most endpoints are available in the major regions; i'll double check the full list but eu-west-1 is fully supported, eu-west-3 sometimes has partial support depending on service. i'll include region mapping in the doc.
[01:45] Liam: what's the egress pattern — do we keep all outbound internet traffic inside our VPC? we have strict egress via NAT and proxy.
[01:52] Maya: with PrivateLink, traffic to redwood flows over the ENI to our service, it doesn't traverse the Internet. for peering it's private as well. If you use our managed control plane, metadata calls might reach Redwood control plane endpoints — we can configure private control plane options for Private deployments so auth and metrics can hit private endpoints.
[02:15] Jordan: customers sometimes want the control plane to be out-of-band — hosted control plane talking to private data plane — we have options.
[02:22] Carlos: latency is a concern — our application needs sub 150ms 95p for short prompts, and some LLM workloads are latency-sensitive. how does private compare to Dedicated?
[02:33] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable latency; Private in your VPC gives similar performance but depends on network hops and peering topology. if you keep everything in the same region and avoid NAT hairpins, latency should be comparable. we do continuous batching and kv cache management — the KV cache (sometimes transcribed as 'K V cash' — apologies) helps with context reuse.
[02:55] Priya: regarding keys — can we bring our own KMS keys / HSM? we have compliance that requires CMKs.
[03:02] Maya: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS and can integrate with your KMS or use a connector to HSM where required. for Private we can ensure keys never leave your account if you prefer — i'll include architecture notes.
[03:16] Liam: what about audit logs? retention? we need 1 year of immutable audit logs for some regulators.
[03:23] Jordan: we provide audit logs, and enterprise plans can get longer retention. logs can be pushed to your S3 or to a SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch. Priya, is S3 export acceptable?
[03:35] Priya: S3 export is fine as long as it's encrypted with our key and access-controlled. also need role-based access and SSO integration.
[03:42] Maya: we have SAML/SSO and RBAC support; for private deployments we integrate into your IdP so roles map to your internal perms.
[03:50] Carlos: circling back to network — we're worried about IP exhaustion in our VPC; do you require lots of ENIs or IPs per instance?
[03:58] Maya: PrivateLink uses ENIs in the consumer VPC; the IP footprint is modest, usually a couple IPs per AZ per service endpoint. for large scale single-tenant Dedicated instances we might need larger subnets but we'll size with your team's numbers — for POC we recommend a small pool and we'll test.
[04:18] Liam: cross-region peering — is that supported? we have eu-west-1 prime, but some teams in us-east-1 need access.
[04:25] Maya: native VPC peering does not support cross-region peering in the classic sense — you can create inter-region peering but it's more complex and costs more. Transit Gateway supports multi-region with attachments and is the usual pattern. PrivateLink also can be set up per region per endpoint. we can propose a hybrid: keep latency-critical in eu-west-1, use a fallback region in us-east-1 for throughput.
[04:50] Carlos: okay. can we self-host the whole stack on-prem? some data cannot leave our network for regulatory reasons.
[04:56] Jordan: Redwood Private supports on-prem packages and air-gapped deployments in enterprise contracts. we have customers who run the data plane in their on-prem clusters and the control plane can be either on-prem or hosted. that'll be part of the enterprise conversation.
[05:10] Priya: do you have SOC 2 type II and ISO? and do you do monthly pen tests?
[05:15] Jordan: yes SOC 2 Type II, ISO is in progress, and we do regular third-party pen-tests — the pack will include certificates and summary.
[05:22] Liam: network ACLs, security groups — how is traffic from our VPC restricted to only the Redwood endpoints?
[05:28] Maya: you can lock down SGs and only allow traffic to the PrivateLink ENI or peered CIDR. we also support mTLS between services for an additional layer.
[05:36] Carlos: one more about performance — what's the burst capacity? say we have a sudden spike from a feature launch.
[05:42] Maya: for Private we can size autoscaling policies — we support burst capacity and can pre-warm nodes. Dedicated has contractual SLAs for throughput; Private within your VPC depends on the compute you provision but we can offer assistance configuring auto-scaling policies.
[05:58] Priya: regulatory question: can we force logs and metrics to stay in eu data stores?
[06:03] Maya: yes, with Private deployments you control the storage endpoints; we'll configure and ensure metrics and logs are stored in your regional S3 or internal stores.
[06:12] Jordan: okay let's talk about the POC scope — Carlos, what are you prioritizing?
[06:16] Carlos: we want to validate latency for our shortest prompts (customer greetings), test throughput for batched embeddings for search, and validate network setup (peering or PrivateLink) with KMS integration. timeline — we'd like a 2 week POC in late April if possible.
[06:32] Jordan: we can do that. we'll need CIDR ranges, expected QPS and avg tokens per request, and a contact for ops.
[06:40] Liam: i'll share CIDRs and our transit gateway constraints.
[06:42] Carlos: also cost — rough order of magnitude for Dedicated and Private for a 2 week POC?
[06:48] Jordan: i'll put together a preliminary pricing sheet — usually POC uses a smaller reserved pool or spot-backed capacity; we'll share both hosted and dedicated numbers.
[06:56] Priya: one more — encryption in transit, do you support customer TLS certs?
[07:01] Maya: yes, we support TLS with customer certs and mutual TLS for sensitive pipes.
[07:06] Ava: curious about developer experience — will our devs call the same API for hosted and private?
[07:11] Jordan: yes that's one of our differentiators — same API surface. you can pin model versions and the SDK is the same.
[07:18] Carlos: any gotchas for Kubernetes-based on-prem?
[07:22] Maya: we provide helm charts and an operator for on-prem, but there are network prerequisites — persistent volumes for logs, and you need GPU drivers for accelerated inference. we'll include the operator docs.
[07:33] Liam: does Redwood do quantized models on Nvidia A100 or do you recommend different hardware?
[07:39] Maya: we run optimizations across hardware; quantization is model dependent, and the runtime picks kernels per GPU. for high throughput embeddings we often recommend certain instance types; i'll add recommended instance types per workload.
[07:55] Jordan: sounds like good next steps — Maya will send the network runbook and region support matrix, i'll send security pack and pricing, Liam will send CIDRs and constraints. schedule a 30m network deep dive next week.
[08:09] Carlos: yep, thanks everyone.
[08:12] Priya: thanks — expect a security checklist back from us before the POC.
[08:16] Jordan: perfect, we'll follow up in email and post the runbook link.
[08:20] Maya: i'll paste the PrivateLink vs Peering diagram and a quick drawn runbook in the follow-up — and link to the docs site (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-networking)
[08:35] Jordan: any final questions?
[08:37] Liam: none for now.
[08:39] Carlos: all good.
[08:41] Jordan: great, meeting over — notes will be shared.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors and filler words present; some product names were transcribed slightly off (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash) but content is accurate. Shared artifacts referenced during call: security pack (link to shared drive), network diagram (to be sent by Maya), pricing sheet (Jordan).

End of transcript.
